item.title: Classic rock band Kansas adds Pensacola to 2027 tour schedule
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Kansas, the legendary progressive rock band behind hits like "Carry On Wayward Son" and "Dust in the Wind," has announced its first dates for 2027, with a stop scheduled for Pensacola among early tour locations. According to a social media post from music promoter Eric Alper, the band will perform in Pensacola, Orlando, Immolaski, and Rockford…
item.content:encoded:
Kansas, the legendary progressive rock band behind hits like "Carry On Wayward Son" and "Dust in the Wind," has announced its first dates for 2027, with a stop scheduled for Pensacola among early tour locations.

According to a social media post from music promoter Eric Alper, the band will perform in Pensacola, Orlando, Immolaski, and Rockford before appearing at Cruise to the Edge in April. The announcement comes as Kansas continues to tour behind decades of classic material that defined rock radio in the 1970s and '80s.

The band said additional 2027 dates are expected to be announced in the coming weeks. A specific venue and date for the Pensacola show have not yet been disclosed. Fans interested in catching Kansas live should watch for ticket information as the tour schedule fills in.

item.title: Mild overnight conditions at Pensacola beach as rising tide expected Thursday
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Pensacola's coastal waters are running calm this morning with gentle 2.6-foot waves and light easterly winds at 13.6 knots, according to Florida Gulf Signal. Air temperature sat at 85 degrees just after 1 a.m., creating humid overnight conditions typical for late September on the Panhandle. Tide conditions Thursday show a rising pattern, with high…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola's coastal waters are running calm this morning with gentle 2.6-foot waves and light easterly winds at 13.6 knots, according to Florida Gulf Signal. Air temperature sat at 85 degrees just after 1 a.m., creating humid overnight conditions typical for late September on the Panhandle.

Tide conditions Thursday show a rising pattern, with high tide expected around 10:20 a.m. at 1.4 feet and low tide around 7:22 p.m. at 0.8 feet. The modest tidal range means minimal beach erosion or flooding concerns for the area.

Those planning beach activities or water sports should anticipate the typical early morning warmth and stable sea state. The light winds make conditions suitable for most coastal activities through the morning hours.

item.content:encoded:
A 41-year-old Escambia County resident is facing multiple charges following a high-speed pursuit that crossed the state line from Alabama into Florida on Wednesday morning, according to law enforcement reports.

Alabama police initiated the chase, which ultimately ended with the suspect's arrest in Florida. The pursuit spanned across the Alabama-Florida border, drawing response from agencies in both states.

Details about the specific charges and the circumstances that triggered the initial traffic stop have not been fully released. The investigation is ongoing, with coordination between Alabama and Florida law enforcement agencies.

The arrest highlights ongoing interstate coordination between local, state, and federal authorities in the Pensacola area, where jurisdictional boundaries frequently overlap with neighboring Alabama.

item.content:encoded:
Fishermen operating off Pensacola Beach recovered a military drone from the water this week, several days after it went missing during U.S. Air Force testing operations in the area.

The LUCAS drone, a tactical unmanned aircraft used by the Air Force, had been lost during a training exercise. The recovery by local anglers marks the end of what appears to have been a brief search effort for the aircraft.

Details about what caused the drone to crash or the exact timeline of the incident remain limited. The Air Force has not yet released a formal statement about the recovery or what led to the aircraft going down near Pensacola Beach, a frequent testing ground for military aviation operations in Northwest Florida.

item.title: Pleasant Fall Preview Coming to Pensacola Area This Weekend
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Pensacola-area residents can expect a stretch of beautiful weather over the next few days, with temperatures dipping into the comfortable 60s and plenty of sunshine, according to the National Weather Service. Thursday will be mostly sunny with a high near 87 degrees and light northeast winds around 5 mph. That evening, conditions will turn partly…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola-area residents can expect a stretch of beautiful weather over the next few days, with temperatures dipping into the comfortable 60s and plenty of sunshine, according to the National Weather Service.

Thursday will be mostly sunny with a high near 87 degrees and light northeast winds around 5 mph. That evening, conditions will turn partly cloudy with a low around 64—a welcome taste of fall after the summer heat. Friday looks even nicer, with sunny skies and highs near 85 degrees, followed by a mostly clear night and temperatures dropping to around 61.

Saturday will round out the pleasant stretch with mostly sunny conditions and a high near 86 degrees. The combination of lower humidity and cooler overnight lows should make outdoor plans comfortable through the weekend.

item.content:encoded:
Northern Santa Rosa County residents now have a new community gathering space. Allentown Community Park opened this week next to the Allentown Volunteer Fire Department at 9482 Highway 89 in Jay, marking the first public park in the Allentown area.

The new facility includes basketball courts, pickleball courts, and a fitness court, along with dedicated parking areas. According to local reporting, the park represents a significant addition to recreational options for the rural community.

Plans are already in place for future improvements to the park, though specific details on those expansions have not yet been announced. The opening reflects ongoing efforts to enhance quality-of-life amenities in northern Santa Rosa County.

item.content:encoded:
Students across the North Escambia area came together Wednesday morning for the annual See You at the Pole gathering, a student-led prayer event held before school began.

The non-denominational event is organized and led entirely by students, who gathered to pray for their schools, classmates, teachers, government, and the nation. See You at the Pole has become a traditional observance in schools across the country, giving students an opportunity to gather around their school flagpole for a moment of reflection and prayer.

The event reflects a long-standing national tradition that emphasizes student leadership and voluntary participation in faith-based gatherings on school grounds.

Su Chong Han was cited for misdemeanor animal cruelty and trespassing in connection with the incident. According to ECSO, Han allegedly left the dog…
item.content:encoded:
A 70-year-old Cantonment woman is facing animal cruelty and trespassing charges after the Escambia County Sheriff's Office say she left her dog inside a hot vehicle while she was feeding stray cats.

Su Chong Han was cited for misdemeanor animal cruelty and trespassing in connection with the incident. According to ECSO, Han allegedly left the dog unattended in the SUV under conditions that endangered the animal's welfare.

The case remains under investigation by the sheriff's office. Animal cruelty charges in Florida can carry significant penalties, and leaving pets in hot vehicles is a particular concern during warmer months when interior temperatures can reach dangerous levels within minutes.

Fostering Coastal Connections serves as a local resource hub, helping to strengthen family networks and provide practical support to households navigating the foster care system. For shoppers interested in attending, the yard sale runs Saturday — details on location and hours are available through the organization's local contacts.

The expansion marks a major investment in the airport's infrastructure and reflects growing passenger traffic through the facility.…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola International Airport is moving forward with its first phase of construction on a new five-gate terminal in the coming weeks, but airport officials face a significant challenge: where to put all the cars.

The expansion marks a major investment in the airport's infrastructure and reflects growing passenger traffic through the facility. However, the project comes with a practical problem that could affect travelers — the airport's current parking capacity may not be sufficient to handle demand while construction is underway.

According to WKRG News 5, planners are already grappling with solutions to the parking shortage. The airport will need to balance construction progress on the new terminal with maintaining adequate parking for passengers during what could be an extended build-out period.

Details on specific parking mitigation plans and the full timeline for the terminal's completion were not immediately available. Airport officials did not respond immediately to questions about whether temporary parking solutions or alternative transportation options are being considered during the construction phase.

item.title: Why Pensacola and a remote Oregon county share the same time—for one hour a year
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Here's a quirky bit of geography that most Pensacola residents probably don't think about: for one hour every year, our corner of the panhandle operates on the exact same time as Malheur County, deep in eastern Oregon. The reason comes down to regional logistics and history. Malheur County sits in the Mountain time zone—an unusual choice for that…
item.content:encoded:
Here's a quirky bit of geography that most Pensacola residents probably don't think about: for one hour every year, our corner of the panhandle operates on the exact same time as Malheur County, deep in eastern Oregon.

The reason comes down to regional logistics and history. Malheur County sits in the Mountain time zone—an unusual choice for that part of Oregon—because it's positioned to stay synchronized with nearby Boise, Idaho, according to a post making the rounds on social media. Pensacola, meanwhile, observes Central time, aligning with the broader Gulf Coast and much of the South.

That hourly overlap happens during the transition windows around daylight saving time. When one region springs forward or falls back before the other completes its own shift, the clocks momentarily align—a geographical quirk that underscores how time zones in America follow economic and political boundaries as much as they follow longitude.

item.content:encoded:
A jury in Bay Minette is set to begin deliberations Thursday in a capital murder trial involving a Daphne man accused of killing four people, according to WKRG News 5. Closing statements wrapped up Wednesday afternoon, moving the case into the jury phase.

The trial has been underway in Baldwin County Circuit Court. Details about the specific charges, evidence presented, or the defendant's identity were not included in the available reporting.

Capital murder cases in Alabama can result in sentences ranging from life imprisonment to capital punishment, depending on jury findings. The jury's deliberations could extend over several days as they weigh the evidence and testimony presented during the trial.
